findings.quote: Those businesses should consider Wave Starter for $0 or Zoho Books Standard.
findings.problem: Site adapter forbids recommending or advising ('fits people who...', never 'you should'). 'Should consider' is a direct recommendation inside Who This Is Not For. Also 'Companies that need up to 25 user seats' section is directive.
findings.fix: Reword neutrally: 'Wave Starter ($0) and Zoho Books Standard publish higher or no invoice caps.'

findings.quote: Who This Is Not For: ... What Would Change Our Answer: ...
findings.problem: Both required sections are embedded as plain-text labels at the end of the stillBetterFit body instead of headed sections, so they are not H2/H3 headings (heading rule; ToC, schema and heading-keyword checks cannot see them).
findings.fix: Move them into alternatives[] entries with Title Case headings, as the other two pages do.

findings.quote: Zoho Books Standard on annual billing saves $144 a year while providing 3 user seats instead of Xero Early's single-tier limits.
findings.problem: Vague/unsupported: Xero publishes no user cap and 'no per-user license fees'; Zoho Standard 3-user cap and Xero Early limits are not comparable as written.
findings.fix: Say 'Zoho Standard includes 3 users; Xero lists no per-user fees'.

findings.quote: Xero includes bank reconciliation on all plans.
findings.problem: Supported (Reconcile bank transactions appears on all three). Verified: prices, 90% promo (ends Nov 30, code), $5 auto-reconcile, 5.1M customers, 'change to less expensive plan 1 month after upgrading'. QuickBooks (WebFetch, fetch_page 502), FreshBooks, Zoho, Wave and FreeAgent figures and all cost arithmetic replay correctly.

findings.quote: Wave offers ... Wave Pro saves $134 a year compared to Xero Early
findings.problem: Compares a $0-card-fee product subscription to Xero without noting Wave's card fees or Xero's 20-invoice cap; fine as arithmetic but one-sided.
